title: Auth/audit incident follow-up: reduce alert fatigue and fill RBAC v2 telemetry gaps
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
Post-incident analysis (INC-2025-01-auth-audit) highlighted two correlated problems: noisy/low-signal alerts from audit pipelines causing operator alert fatigue, and missing RBAC v2 telemetry fields that prevented rapid root-cause identification for admin-scoped operations. This ticket captures the mitigation work: (1) alert tuning and aggregation to reduce noise, (2) schema and instrumentation changes to guarantee RBAC v2 context (principal_id, role_snapshot, grant_source) in every audit event, and (3) runbook updates and retrospectives to reduce mean time to remediate for future auth incidents.

Goals:
- Reduce actionable alert volume from audit streams by >= 60% without reducing detection of high-severity incidents.
- Ensure >= 99.9% of admin-scoped audit events include RBAC v2 context fields required for triage.
- Ship new alert aggregation rules + updated runbook and validate via canary.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Alert policy changes (observability): aggregate low-importance auth events by actor + resource over 10m windows, convert high-frequency one-off events into summarized incidents, and implement dedupe for repeated SAML failures from the same IP. Update PagerDuty escalation to only trigger for aggregated thresholds or elevated risk tags (admin=true or role:org-admin).
2) Audit schema/enrichment: add guaranteed fields to audit events: principal_id, principal_type, role_snapshot (list of role ids), grant_source (direct|group|inherit), and request_trace_id. Implement in the API gateway and the auth service (authn/authz middleware) and in the RBAC v2 evaluation path.
3) Ingestion and storage: modify audit-event-ingest pipeline to stop dropping events when enrichment is delayed; temporarily buffer and label events with enrichment_pending=true for 24h; implement a job that backfills role_snapshot for buffered events.
4) Runbooks and dashboards: create a single runbook for auth/audit incidents that references the new dedupe/aggregation behavior, escalate play for admin-scope events, and add a dashboard widget showing volume of enrichment_pending events and principal_id missing rates.
5) Canary & rollout: stage changes in dedicated-infra (canary group set) for 14 days, monitor false-positive and false-negative detection rates, then roll to hosted.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Cost: buffering + backfill will temporarily increase storage/compute costs for audit pipeline. We'll limit buffer TTL to 24h and prioritize admin-scoped events.
- Fidelity: summarizing low-risk events reduces raw event availability for ad-hoc forensics; mitigated by retaining raw payloads for admin-scoped and sampled support-user events (1%).
- Complexity: introducing enrichment_pending state requires changes across multiple services; will coordinate via clearly documented API contracts.

Acceptance criteria:
- New aggregated alert config deployed and validated (alert volume drop >= 60% within canary)
- >= 99.9% of admin-scoped events have principal_id and role_snapshot recorded for a 72h window post-rollout
- Runbook accepted by oncall rotation owners and added to Google Drive
- Post-deploy audit playbook walkthrough completed in Ops sync

Links and artifacts:
- Incident writeup: https://go.redwood.com/incidents/INC-2025-01-auth-audit
- Initial postmortem notes: https://docs.redwood.com/confluence/display/AUTH/Auth-Audit-Incident-2025
- Dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/auitauth/alert-triage
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/834
- Pipeline change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/event-ingest/pull/459

comments: 2025-01-20 - Ava Patel: Kicked off initial triage with SRE and Security. Found high churn of SAML_FAILURE events from two legacy SSO integrations; noise was masking admin privilege escalations.

2025-01-22 - Marcus Nguyen: Implemented preliminary alert dedupe rules in a staging Grafana Alertmanager instance. Observed 48% reduction in total alert count for test window; still seeing gaps where principal_id is null.
2025-01-24 - Elena Gomez (Security): Approved schema changes but requested explicit KMS tagging for any logs that include role_snapshot to meet retention policies. Added to scope.
2025-01-28 - Marcus Nguyen: Auth service changes merged (PR 834). Added principal_id propagation through the oauth/saml middleware; initial canary deploy scheduled for 2025-02-01.

2025-02-01 - Oncall rotation (SRE): Canary started against dedicated-infra subset. Early metric: enrichment_pending spikes to 0.7% of events due to a race condition; created ENG-51250 to address backfill job retry logic.
2025-02-02 - Priya Shah (QA): Runbook draft uploaded to Google Drive; requested additional screenshots for new dashboard panels. Marked runbook review for 2025-02-05 Ops sync.
